post.summary: Run a workflow via the orchestrator (JSON or multipart with file uploads)
post.description: Accepts `application/json` with `{ conversationId, message, inputs?, config?, tiers?, aliases? }` or `multipart/form-data` with `conversationId`, `message`, optional `inputs` and `config` fields holding their objects JSON-encoded, optional `tiers` and `aliases` JSON object fields, and optional file attachments (max 5 files, 10 MB each). `inputs` supplies values for the workflow's declared `inputs:` (#2554); it is validated against the declaration before any worktree, clone, or AI cost, so a missing required input or an undeclared key is refused up front. `config` supplies a sparse runtime layer; `tiers` and `aliases` rebind named model presets above it. Caller-supplied filesystem config paths are rejected. JSON requests may supply `adopt_run_id` or `supersedes_run_id`, but not both. Unique prefixes resolve in the conversation selected project; full IDs select the exact run. Missing project scope for a prefix, unknown or ambiguous IDs, and non-terminal targets return HTTP 400 before queuing; ambiguity errors list candidates. Execution rechecks targets after queuing. If dispatch would continue an existing run, either declaration is refused before continuation or its fresh fallback. Execution-time refusals arrive on conversation SSE after an HTTP 200 accepted response. The refusal names the existing run: resume it with `/workflow resume <id>`, abandon it with `/workflow abandon <id>` before retrying, or use a conversation with no open run. An accepted fresh supersede records `adopted_from_run_id` and `metadata.continuation.mode: "supersede"` on the new run.

get.description: Walks the run's artifact directory and returns relative file paths with size + mtime. Drives the console Artifacts tab. Leaves out only the engine's own `.archon` child at the root, the same rule `archon workflow get` applies; a workflow's own dotfiles are listed. Resolves for every project kind — `owner/repo`, `_local/<basename>`, and `_folder/<slug>` — preferring the run's persisted `output_root` and re-deriving from the codebase when it is absent or no longer inside ARCHON_HOME. Returns `{ files: [] }` only when the location resolved and the run genuinely wrote nothing; returns 404 when the output location cannot be resolved at all.
